scope: Compare the unchanged endpoint/P4 native parent with a DRC executable/test-process Rust allocator change. Mathematical sources and reusable-library allocator ownership remain unchanged.
review_findings: mimalloc 0.1.52 implements GlobalAlloc through aligned mi_malloc, mi_zalloc, mi_realloc and mi_free. Its default feature set is empty and it forwards explicitly selected features to libmimalloc-sys.

libmimalloc-sys 0.1.49 builds vendored v3 by default through cc, with release debug assertions disabled. The override feature alone enables process C-malloc replacement; it is not enabled by this trial. Native C allocations outside Rust GlobalAlloc may remain with their original allocator.

The build script has OS/compiler-specific paths for Unix TLS, MSVC C++ atomics, Windows system libraries and Linux ARM atomics. This first executable trial runs on the current Linux host. Other runtime platforms remain unverified; wasm family targets retain their current allocator.

DRC has a thin CLI main and reusable library. The candidate installs the allocator only in the CLI crate root and under cfg(test) in the standalone library unit-test root. Library consumers, integration-test drivers and doctests retain their own allocator.
The profile allocator subset occupies 29.580% of sampled cycle weight. Its categories include more than Rust global allocation, and it is not predicted savings.

variants.baseline: Unchanged parent plus two shared allocator contract tests; default process allocator.
variants.candidate: Identical parent and shared tests, plus the pinned mimalloc dependency and process-owned global allocator module for native-family CLI/unit-test binaries.

qualification: Verify exact source delta, locked metadata, vendored dependency checksums and identical shared tests.

Both variants: formatting; two allocator contract tests; all-feature DRC tests including integration/doc tests with only the two original gates executed separately; strict all-target DRC Clippy with default and all features; warning-denied DRC docs; release CLI and test builds.
Inspect allocator selection in both built CLI and unit-test executables and confirm mimalloc/libmimalloc-sys were compiled without override or other extra features.
Run both original complete-fixture assertion tests for both variants. Preserve baseline gate failures and stop admission if either candidate assertion fails.

fixed_application_design_if_candidate_ga.timing: Fresh CLI processes, same extracted absolute input paths, original four checks and 0.0762 minimum width. Whole-process wall and user/system CPU are application measurements, not replacements for original internal assertions.
fixed_application_design_if_candidate_ga.memory: Maximum process RSS from the same uninstrumented CLI run, in KiB. This includes allocator overhead/retention but is not requested/live payload or allocation traffic.
fixed_application_design_if_candidate_ga.output: Every full report must match complete bytes and JSON values without field normalization. Freeze every executable before any measurement. Retain all samples, including startup adverse rows; do not extend/filter a closed set.
fixed_application_design_if_candidate_ga.size: Record CLI and unit-test executable byte sizes.

risk_review: The allocator changes address reuse, cross-thread free behavior, binary size, startup and peak resident memory. Shared safe-Rust controls exercise alignment, zeroing, reallocation contents and cross-thread Arc destruction; native tests and complete reports exercise application behavior.
Only DRC unit tests and CLI actually select the candidate allocator. Do not claim that separately linked kernel tests, integration drivers or doctests use it.
Existing parent scalar/native tradeoffs, complete workflow matrix, other platforms and full properties/targets/future-work obligations remain open.
